source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source_reported_historical_synonyms: Vicia ludoviciana var. texana (Torr. & A. Gray) Shinners

morphology_source_reported.peduncles: Flowers open after peduncle elongates; mostly 3–8.5 cm long in flower, usually longer than half subtending leaf; elongates little in fruit
morphology_source_reported.corolla_color: Pinkish white to deep bluish purple
morphology_source_reported.fruiting_peduncles: Approximately same length as in flowering stage [p.707]

habitat_source_reported: Rocky or sandy soils, open woods and roadsides
cautions: 1999 Flora treats subsp. ludoviciana, inventory has variety-level record; keep historic rank separation explicit
Taxon concepts require independent name reconciliation before identification scoring
Regional occurrence is not evidence of local BONAP nativity
Peduncle length comparison must use flowering vs fruiting stage, not single raw length; the two subspecies intergrade.
Kew accepts the autonymic variety; Flora's subsp. ludoviciana traits remain attached to the 1999 concept until morphological equivalence is established.
